title: Disagreeing well
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: -(neu)ndeyo LAYS DOWN A BACKGROUND AND STOPS. Joeundeyo is not it is good; it is it is good, but... with the but deleted, and the deletion is the politeness. No English punctuation renders it, so the literal line says it in words.

jom eoryeoul geot gatayo IS A REFUSAL. It is not a difficulty rating and it leaves no opening. Heard as it might be a bit hard, so there is still a chance, it has been misread, and that misreading survives every correction about grammar.

ENGLISH MARKS REFUSAL LEXICALLY: no, I cannot. Korean marks it by understatement plus an unfinished clause, and the same understatement in English would mean the opposite. The hedging words map one to one; the pragmatics do not.

TWO ENDINGS THAT LOOK ALIKE. -(eu)lji, uncertainty, is written attached: halji, galji, olji. L4-M6's -(eu)n ji, elapsed time, is a bound noun with a space in front of it. This module writes only the attached one.

THIS ENDING IS NOT L1-M10's geureonde. The standalone connective sits between two finished sentences; the ending lives on a stem and finishes nothing. Same syllables, different word, and this module never writes the standalone one.

THE SHAPE OF THE ENDING FOLLOWS THE STEM. An adjective takes -(eu)ndeyo: joeundeyo, bappeundeyo. An action verb takes -neundeyo: ilhaneundeyo. isseoyo and eopseoyo go with the action verbs, which gives eomneundeyo.
geot gatayo IS L3-M3's, REUSED AND NOT REOPENED. On a future -(eu)l stem it guesses at what will happen, and the guess is what does the refusing. gatayo never appears on its own.
THE FLAT CONTRADICTION IS NOT TAUGHT HERE. L3-M3's teullyeoyo stays a pointer: this module exists because the flat contradiction is what NOT to say. No banmal, and no -(seu)pnida, which is L4-M7's.

sentences.cue: This one is really good, but...

words.note: joayo with the trailing -(eu)ndeyo. It is not it is good; it is it is good, but... with the but left out, and leaving it out is the politeness.

sentences.trap: The praise is the hedge. A learner who hears only joeundeyo has heard a compliment and missed the objection that was never spoken.
sentences.sound: i-GEO-ga JEONG-mal JO-eun-de-yo. The last syllable trails off and does not fall the way a finished sentence does.

variations.display: I-geo-ga jeongmal joeundeyo... Geunde jom bissayo.
variations.script: 이거가 정말 좋은데요... 근데 좀 비싸요.
variations.cue: This one is really good, but it is a bit expensive.
variations.changed: the deleted half spoken out loud, which is blunter

variations.cue: This one is really good, but...
variations.changed: -neun instead of -ga, marking it as the topic

mistake.why: Dropping the -yo drops the politeness with it. The ending taught here is -(eu)ndeyo, and the yo is not optional anywhere in this course.

sentences.usage: Turning down a suggestion in a shop without saying no.

sentences.cue: I am a bit busy right now, but...

words.note: The same ending on bappayo, whose stem is bappeu-. Said with the voice trailing off, it declines an invitation without the word no ever appearing.

sentences.trap: jom is not a measure of how busy. It is the softener that makes the refusal polite, and removing it makes the same sentence a complaint.
sentences.sound: JI-geu-meun JOM ba-PPEUN-de-yo. The double p is held, and the ending trails away.

variations.cue: I am a bit busy right now, but how about tomorrow?
variations.changed: an alternative offered after the trailing clause

variations.cue: I am a bit busy today, but...
variations.changed: today rather than right now

mistake.why: Finished, this is a statement of fact and nothing follows from it. The trailing ending is what leaves the refusal unsaid and the other person's face intact.

sentences.usage: Deflecting a request at your desk.
sentences.mnemonic: Trail off and the no is understood.

sentences.cue: I am working right now, but...

words.note: An ACTION verb takes -neundeyo, not -(eu)ndeyo: ilha- plus the ending. It lays down what you are doing and lets the listener draw the conclusion.

sentences.trap: The two shapes are not free variants. joeundeyo is an adjective's and ilhaneundeyo is an action verb's, and swapping them is the commonest slip in this module.
sentences.sound: JEO-neun JI-geum IL-ha-neun-de-yo. ilha- runs together; the h is light between the vowels.

variations.cue: I am working today, but...
variations.changed: today rather than right now

variations.cue: I am working here right now, but...
variations.changed: the place added in front of the ending

mistake.why: An action verb takes -neundeyo straight on the stem: ilha- plus the ending. The -(eu)ndeyo that gives joeundeyo belongs to adjectives.

sentences.usage: Fending off an interruption without refusing outright.

sentences.cue: Well, I think it will be expensive.

words.note: The non-committal opener. It commits to nothing and buys the sentence after it, and it is a whole turn on its own when nothing else is safe to say.
bissayo under the -(eu)l modifier, waiting for L3-M3's geot gatayo. The future modifier is what turns a description into a guess.

sentences.trap: geulsseyo is not yes and not no. Answered with it, a proposal has been declined politely, and a learner who hears maybe has misheard.
sentences.sound: geul-SSE-yo, bi-SSAL GEOT GA-ta-yo. The ss of geulsseyo is tensed and held.

variations.display: Geulsseyo, bissal geot gatayo. Dareun geo-reul boseyo.
variations.script: 글쎄요, 비쌀 것 같아요. 다른 거를 보세요.
variations.cue: Well, I think it will be expensive. Have a look at another one.
variations.changed: a suggestion added after the hedge

variations.cue: Well, I think it will be a bit expensive.
variations.changed: jom added, which softens it further

mistake.why: geot cannot be dropped. L3-M3's frame is the two-word geot gatayo, and gatayo never stands on its own after a modifier.

sentences.usage: Answering a price question you would rather not answer.
sentences.mnemonic: geulsseyo buys time and gives ground.

sentences.display: Geulsseyo, naeil-eun bi-ga ol geot gatayo.
sentences.script: 글쎄요, 내일은 비가 올 것 같아요.
sentences.cue: Well, I think it will rain tomorrow.
sentences.literal: well, tomorrow-TOP rain-SUBJ come-will thing seems

words.note: The -(eu)l modifier of wayo. With bi-ga in front and geot gatayo after it, this is the ordinary way to talk about weather you cannot vouch for.

sentences.trap: Used against somebody's plan, this is a disagreement and not a forecast. The weather is the reason the plan will not happen.
sentences.sound: geul-SSE-yo, NAE-i-reun BI-ga OL GEOT GA-ta-yo. ol is one short beat with a clear l.

variations.display: Geulsseyo, naeil-eun bi-ga an ol geot gatayo.
variations.script: 글쎄요, 내일은 비가 안 올 것 같아요.
variations.cue: Well, I think it will not rain tomorrow.
variations.changed: the guess turned negative

variations.display: Geulsseyo, oneul-eun bi-ga ol geot gatayo.
variations.script: 글쎄요, 오늘은 비가 올 것 같아요.
variations.cue: Well, I think it will rain today.
variations.changed: today rather than tomorrow

mistake.why: wayo asserts it. The point of the hedge is that the speaker is not asserting, and ol geot gatayo leaves the other person room to disagree.

sentences.usage: Casting doubt on an outdoor plan without vetoing it.
sentences.mnemonic: Guess at the weather, not at the person.

sentences.cue: I could not say whether I will go tomorrow.

words.note: -(eu)lji written attached, one word, on any stem: galji, halji. L4-M6's elapsed-time ji is a separate bound noun with a space, and the two are never spelled alike.

sentences.trap: moreugesseoyo after -(eu)lji is a hedge, not an admission. It declines to commit; it does not confess ignorance.
sentences.sound: NAE-il GAL-ji mo-reu-GE-sseo-yo. galji is one word with no pause inside it.

variations.cue: I could not say whether I will do it tomorrow.
variations.changed: the same ending on hada

variations.cue: I could not say whether I will go today.
variations.changed: today rather than tomorrow

mistake.why: Written with a space, ji is L4-M6's bound noun for elapsed time. The uncertainty ending is one word: galji.

sentences.usage: Keeping an invitation open without accepting it.

sentences.cue: I could not say whether my friend will come.

words.note: The same ending on wayo. Followed by moreugesseoyo it is I could not say, which is a hedge about somebody else and never a complaint about them.

sentences.trap: The subject here is somebody else, and that is allowed: -(eu)lji is about the not-knowing, so it can be used of anyone.
sentences.sound: CHIN-gu-ga OL-ji mo-reu-GE-sseo-yo. olji keeps its l before the j.

variations.cue: I could not say whether the doctor will come.
variations.changed: the doctor rather than a friend

variations.cue: I could not say whether my friend will come tomorrow.
variations.changed: the day added

mistake.why: omyeon is L3-M4's if, which builds a condition. -(eu)lji makes the whole clause the thing that is not known: olji moreugesseoyo.

sentences.usage: Answering for someone else without promising anything.

sentences.cue: I am sorry, but there is no time right now, so...

words.note: eopseoyo takes the action-verb ending -neundeyo, and the p becomes m in front of the n. This course writes what is said, as it writes masinneun.

sentences.trap: joesonghajiman opens the refusal and the trailing ending closes it without a verb. The two together are the whole no, and neither one says it.
sentences.sound: joe-SONG-ha-ji-man, JI-geu-meun SI-ga-ni EOM-neun-de-yo. eops- is heard as eom before the n.

variations.cue: I am sorry, but there is no time today, so...
variations.changed: today rather than right now

variations.cue: There is no time right now, so...
variations.changed: the apology dropped, which is less deferential

mistake.why: The p of eops- becomes m in front of the n, and this course romanizes what is said: eomneundeyo, on the same rule that gives masinneun.

sentences.usage: Declining a request from someone senior.
sentences.mnemonic: eops- meets n and comes out eom.

sentences.display: Joesonghajiman, jeo-neun dareun geo-ga deo joeundeyo...
sentences.script: 죄송하지만, 저는 다른 거가 더 좋은데요...
sentences.cue: I am sorry, but I prefer a different one, so...
sentences.literal: sorry-but, I-TOP different thing-SUBJ more good-but-and-then-nothing

words.note: The modifier for another one of the same kind. In front of geo it offers an alternative, which is how a disagreement here stays an offer rather than a rejection.

sentences.trap: Offering the alternative is the disagreement. Naming what is wrong with the first one would be the flat contradiction this module exists to avoid.
sentences.sound: joe-SONG-ha-ji-man, JEO-neun DA-reun GEO-ga DEO JO-eun-de-yo.

variations.cue: I am sorry, but a different one is better, so...
variations.changed: the speaker left out, which is the ordinary shape

variations.display: Joesonghajiman, jeo-neun jom dareun geo-ga joeundeyo...
variations.script: 죄송하지만, 저는 좀 다른 거가 좋은데요...
variations.cue: I am sorry, but I like a somewhat different one, so...
variations.changed: jom in front, which softens it further

mistake.display: Joesonghajiman, jeo-neun dareun geo-ga deo joayo.
mistake.script: 죄송하지만, 저는 다른 거가 더 좋아요.
mistake.why: Finished with joayo it is a flat statement of preference. The trailing joeundeyo leaves the disagreement unspoken, which is what joesonghajiman promised.

sentences.usage: Disagreeing with a recommendation from a shop assistant.
sentences.mnemonic: Offer the other one; never name the fault.

sentences.cue: The timing would be a bit difficult. (No.)

words.note: The -(eu)l modifier of eoryeoweoyo. jom eoryeoul geot gatayo is a refusal; the present eoryeoun would only rate how hard the thing is.

sentences.trap: This is the module. It is a no, it leaves no opening, and a learner who reads it as there is still a chance has made the most expensive mistake in the course.
sentences.sound: SI-ga-ni JOM eo-RYEO-ul GEOT GA-ta-yo. The whole sentence stays low and even; no word is pushed.

variations.cue: Tomorrow would be a bit difficult. (No.)
variations.changed: the day refused rather than the timing

variations.cue: The timing is a bit difficult.
variations.changed: said outright, which is heard as blunter than the hedge

mistake.why: eoryeoun is the present modifier and reads as a description of how hard something is. The refusal needs the future -(eu)l: eoryeoul geot gatayo.

sentences.usage: Turning down a meeting time you cannot make.
